text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Syria demands a freeze on normalisation with Israel. Arab League meets today in Cairo. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to aides: Our relations with Egypt "a chronic disease".
- Israeli army order for soldiers to get more sleep.
- Danger: Palestinian sewage pollutes Israeli drinking water.
MAARIV

- Jordanian Prime Minister Kabariti, in interview with Maariv, says: Netanyahu tells us one thing -- and does the opposite. We very much wanted to believe Netanyahu -- but the more time passes, the more we are disappointed and bewildered."
- Blind baby brought from Syria for an operation at Hadassah hospital begins to see.
JERUSALEM POST
- Jews, Arabs clash in Hebron. No serious injuries reported.
- Cabinet ministers angry at prime minister for keeping them in the dark on Hebron.
- Netanyahu, Palestinian President Arafat deny they will meet in Lisbon.
- Netanyahu plans visit to Russia early next year.
- Netanyahu, Egyptian President Mubarak clash over settlements.
- Intermarriage in cards for U.S. Jewry.
HAARETZ
- Syria launches pressure campaign on Arab states to suspend normalisation with Israel.
- Since discovery of AIDS there have been 1,464 carriers located in Israel and 423 patients.
- Intelligence experts now believe it will take a much shorter time than previously for Iran to develop a nuclear bomb -- 10 years is overly optimistic.
- Shin Bet security service prevents hiring of Arabs as waiters and cooks at events in which VIPs take part.
- New way to cut two billion shekels: each cabinet minister will decide what to cut from his ministry.
